transcript.content: Hello, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I came in because my head’s been feeling kind of foggy. I’m making little mistakes in my client notes at work and forgetting what I was about to do, and that’s not really like me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Yeah… I have. Lately I’ve been waking up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I can still get through my shift and talk to people, but inside I just feel sad and kind of flat.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I still do things if I have to, but I haven’t paid much attention to whether I’m enjoying them less. It’s more like I’ve just been feeling kind of off.
Have you been enjoying things less than you usually do?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear loss of enjoyment, exactly. I guess I just feel off, but I can’t say for sure that things feel less enjoyable than usual.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?
Yeah, my sleep’s been kind of all over the place. Some nights I’m just lying there thinking about family stuff, and other times I wake up before my alarm and can’t really get back to sleep.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot?
I don’t know if I’d say a lot. I’ve had things on my mind, but I’m not sure it’s more than usual worrying.
Have you been using alcohol or drugs more than usual lately?
Not really. I haven’t noticed myself drinking or using anything more than I usually would.
Has something particularly stressful happened in your life recently?
Yeah… my uncle died about two weeks ago. I’d say that’s when this whole shift really started.
Do your sadness and mental fog feel mainly connected to your uncle’s death?
Yeah, I think so. This whole shift really seemed to start after my uncle died, about two weeks ago.
Since your uncle died, have you been feeling guilty about things that aren’t really about his death?
Yeah… mostly it’s about him. I keep going over what I should’ve done for my tío before he died—like calling him more, or visiting sooner. Then I start feeling like I failed him as family.
Since your uncle died, have you found yourself really longing or yearning for him?
I don’t know if I’d call it yearning exactly. I miss him, yeah… but I haven’t really noticed it as this strong longing. It’s more like I think about him and feel sad.
Since your uncle died, have you noticed your appetite has changed?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close attention to it, but I don’t think I’ve noticed any big change in my appetite.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
Yeah, I have. My head feels kind of foggy, and I keep making little mistakes in my client notes or forgetting what I was about to do. That’s not really like me.
Have you gotten confused about where you were or what day it was?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve been forgetful and distracted, but I haven’t been confused about where I am or what day it is.
Have you had any thoughts that կյանք isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
I’m not planning to hurt myself. But… yeah, there have been some mornings where I think maybe it wouldn’t be the worst thing if I just didn’t wake up. That scares me to even say.
Since your uncle died, have you clearly lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I don’t know if I’d say clearly. I mean, I haven’t really been paying close attention to that. Some things feel harder to get into lately, but I’m not sure if it’s loss of interest or just… everything feeling heavier.
Have other people noticed that you’ve been moving or speaking more slowly than usual lately?
I haven’t really noticed anyone saying that. I don’t think I’ve been moving or talking slower than usual, at least not that I’m aware of.
Have these symptoms started to interfere with how well you’re functioning at work or in your day-to-day life?

Yeah, a bit. At work I’ve had to ask coworkers to double-check my client notes and documentation because I’m missing details. And at home, my wife has taken over some of the bills and scheduling stuff because I’m just not as reliable with keeping track of it right now.
Since your uncle died, have there been moments when something good happens and your mood actually lifts, even briefly?
I’m not really sure. I mean, if something nice happens I might feel okay for a little bit, but I haven’t really been tracking whether my mood lifts in a noticeable way.
Since this started, have you clearly been enjoying the things you usually like less than before?
I’m not sure I’d say clearly. I’ve still done some of the things I usually like, and they’re okay, but I haven’t really paid close attention to whether I’m enjoying them less than before.

final_diagnosis.reason: Symptoms began within about 2 weeks of a clear psychosocial stressor (uncle’s death) and are described as mainly connected to that loss. The patient has low mood, insomnia, concentration problems, guilt related to the deceased, passive death wishes, and mild functional impairment, but the presentation does not clearly establish a full major depressive episode because loss of interest is not confirmed and the syndrome appears stress-linked and temporally limited. Cognitive symptoms are better explained by grief-related distress and depressed mood than by a primary memory disorder; insomnia is present but not the primary diagnosis.
